summary: Defect density rises monotonically with dose from dose 1 to dose 3, then dose 4 leaves the regime where the D/G ratio gives a defect density. Dose 1 to 3 is stage 1 (isolated point defects): I_D/I_G at 532 nm goes 0.25 to 0.57 to 1.19, which gives inter-defect distances L_D of about 24, 15.5 and 10.3 nm, or point-defect densities of roughly 5.6e10, 1.3e11 and 3.0e11 cm^-2 (from the 1e14/(pi L_D^2) conversion, unverified in the source text). Dose 4 shows stage-2 signatures (G band 1591 cm^-1, FWHM 45 cm^-1 versus 14 cm^-1, 2D band lost, D/G falling back to 0.58), so its D/G ratio is past the maximum and cannot be converted to a defect density by the stage-1 relation. Dose 4 must be on the high-density branch, whose stage-1 root would be L_D ~1.2 nm (n_D ~2e13 cm^-2), but that is outside the relation's validity. The Raman-based numbers rest on one stated assumption: the Cancado et al. 2011 stage-1 model with C_A = 160/E_L^4, which carries about ±30% uncertainty.

observations.finding: Raman bands fit cleanly with Lorentzians: D at 1346-1352 cm^-1, G at 1580.3-1580.6 cm^-1 in doses 1-3, 2D at 2689.8-2690.9 cm^-1 in doses 1-3. Residual RMS 49-71 counts, consistent with the measured noise of about 45-70 counts.
Height ratio I_D/I_G rises monotonically from dose 1 to dose 3: 0.250 -> 0.569 -> 1.191, then falls to 0.575 at dose 4.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian heights, 68% Monte Carlo from fit covariance: dose1 0.250 [0.242, 0.258]; dose2 0.569 [0.561, 0.577]; dose3 1.191 [1.179, 1.203]; dose4 0.575 [0.559, 0.592]. Area ratios: 0.263, 0.599, 1.256, 0.752. Fit-only errors are below 2%; the dominant uncertainty is model choice.

observations.finding: The G band stays constant in position and width across doses 1-3 (stage-1 signature), then changes strongly at dose 4 (stage 2): G up-shifts by about 11 cm^-1 and broadens from 14 to 45 cm^-1, and the 2D band disappears.
observations.evidence: G FWHM 14.0, 13.9, 13.9, 44.9 cm^-1; G position 1580.3, 1580.6, 1580.4, 1591.4 cm^-1; I_2D/I_G 3.02 [3.00, 3.05], 2.98 [2.96, 3.00], 2.97 [2.95, 3.00], 0.09 [0.03, 0.15] (dose4 2D is a broad hump about 200 counts above noise, not a fitted band). Si calibration is 520.88-520.91 cm^-1 in all spectra, a stable offset of about +0.2 cm^-1, so the 11 cm^-1 shift is not calibration.
observations.source: Cancado et al., Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011), arXiv:1105.0175: Fig. 5(c) states that Gamma_G stays roughly constant until stage 2 and the caption ties this to the onset of amorphization stage

observations.finding: Converted to inter-defect distance with the stage-1 model at 532 nm, the three stage-1 spectra give L_D = 23.9, 15.5 and 10.3 nm, i.e. n_D = 5.6e10, 1.3e11 and 3.0e11 cm^-2.
observations.evidence: E_L = 2.331 eV; C_A = 160/E_L^4 = 5.42 eV^4 (+/-1.63); r_S = 1 nm, r_A = 3.1 nm, C_S = 0; I_D/I_G = C_A[exp(-pi r_S^2/L^2) - exp(-pi r_A^2/L^2)]. Ranges with C_A +/-30%: dose1 20.2-26.9 nm, dose2 12.9-17.7 nm, dose3 8.3-11.9 nm. n_D from 1e14/(pi L_D^2) with L_D in nm.
observations.source: Cancado et al., Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011), arXiv:1105.0175: Fig. 3 caption (C_A = (160 +/- 48) E_L^-4, r_A = 3.1 nm, r_S = 1 nm, C_S = 0), Fig. 4 caption (E_L^4 I_D/I_G versus L_D). n_D = 1e14/(pi L_D^2) was not found in the parsed text and is from memory, unverified.

observations.finding: The stage-1 relation is valid only for L_D above about 2 r_A = 6.2 nm. Dose 3 (L_D ~10 nm) is inside that range, but near its lower edge.
observations.evidence: Validity sentence: 'In this regime, where L_D > 2r_A ...'. Fig. 4 mentions L_D >= 10 nm as the defect-density regime of most of the data. Dose 3 range 8.3-11.9 nm straddles the stated 10 nm benchmark.
observations.source: Cancado et al., Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011), arXiv:1105.0175: text paragraph on the L_D > 2r_A regime; Fig. 4 caption/text.

observations.finding: The I_D/I_G maximum at L_D ~3 nm makes a single ratio ambiguous, so the G-width is needed to choose the branch. For doses 1-3 the G width is constant at 14 cm^-1, which selects the low-density branch; dose 4's broad G band points to the other (high-density) branch.
observations.evidence: Model maximum at L_D = 3.46 nm (f_max = 3.74). Dose 3 ratio 1.19 has a second root near L_D ~1.2 nm on the high-density branch; dose 4 ratio 0.575 has root L_D ~1.18 nm, n_D ~2e13 cm^-2, outside the model's validity.
observations.source: Cancado et al., Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011), arXiv:1105.0175: abstract (maximum at inter-defect distance ~3 nm; G-width and dispersion resolve the two branches).

observations.finding: The D' band is weak. I_D/I_G' is 0.042, 0.092, 0.173 for doses 1-3, and I_D/I_D' is about 6-7 across doses 1-3 (dose4 ~14, unreliable because D' is weak and overlaps the G shoulder).
observations.evidence: D' heights 119, 331, 433 counts; D heights 702, 2046, 2971. I_D/I_D': dose1 5.9, dose2 6.2, dose3 6.9. D' heights are close to the noise level for dose 1.

observations.finding: I_D/I_D' of about 6-7 is closest to the vacancy-like value, but the attribution is tentative.
observations.evidence: Eckmann et al. abstract: I_D/I_D' ~13 for sp3 defects, ~7 for vacancy-like defects, ~3.5 for boundaries in graphite.
observations.source: Eckmann et al., Nano Lett. 12, 3925 (2012), arXiv:1207.2058 (abstract only; the laser wavelength behind those values was not checked).

observations.finding: There is no evidence of doping or strain change over doses 1-3: the G position is constant at 1580.3-1580.6 cm^-1, the 2D position at 2689.8-2690.9, I_2D/I_G at 2.97-3.02, and 2D FWHM at 32 cm^-1.
observations.evidence: Values from the fits above; position scatter 0.3-0.5 cm^-1 is comparable to the 0.2 cm^-1 calibration offset.

caveats: The Raman defect densities depend on the stage-1 model C_A = (160 +/- 48)/E_L^4 with r_S = 1 nm and r_A = 3.1 nm, taken from the Fig. 3 caption of arXiv:1105.0175. C_A carries about 30% uncertainty, which moves L_D by about 20% and dominates the error budget. The fit errors alone are below 2%.

The n_D = 1e14/(pi L_D^2) conversion is from memory and was not located in the parsed Cancado et al. text, so the absolute densities should be treated as order-of-magnitude until checked against the paper.

I used peak heights for the intensity ratio. Area ratios differ by 5-10% (0.26, 0.60, 1.26, 0.75), which does not change the stage assignment. Whether the source model uses heights or areas was not verified.

Dose 1's D band is weak (about 700 counts above a baseline near 700-1000 counts). The 0.25 ratio, and so the 24 nm L_D, depends on the baseline model. A different baseline could move it substantially.

Background level differs strongly between spectra (about 700-1000 counts in dose 1, about 300 at low shift in dose 4). Intensity ratios within one spectrum are robust to this; absolute intensities are not comparable across doses.

Only one laser wavelength was used, so the G-band dispersion test that resolves the two branches cannot be applied. The stage assignment for doses 1-3 relies on the constant G width and position, and for dose 4 on the large G shift and broadening, not on dispersion.
The dose-4 2D band is not resolved (about 200 counts above noise). Its I_2D/I_G of 0.09 is an upper-limit-like value. The 2D width of 177 cm^-1 is a fit artifact, not a measurement.
A single-point spike near 2150 cm^-1 in dose2 is an artifact outside the fitted windows. It was not analysed and does not affect the results.

I could not use the ramanlens skill's helper scripts and reference notes, because they sit outside the working folder, which I am restricted to. The analysis used my own numpy/lmfit scripts instead. The reference notes were not consulted, so the material-specific guidance in them is missing from this report.

questions_for_user: Which laser wavelength and objective NA did the 2011 Cancado et al. calibration use for the C_A coefficient? I assumed the 532 nm relation via E_L^-4 scaling; confirming that the 514.5 nm dataset in that paper applies unchanged to your setup would tighten the 30% uncertainty.

Were the four spectra acquired with identical integration time, accumulation, and grating? The baseline differs by about 3x between dose 1 and dose 4, and I need to know whether this is fluorescence/background or a change in acquisition.

What were the doses in physical units (ion fluence, plasma time, or similar)? A dose-to-defect-density calibration would let the Raman numbers be cross-checked against an independent method such as AFM or XPS.
Was the dose-4 spectrum measured at the same spot as the other three? If the damage was localised, a spatial map would separate the stage-1 and stage-2 regions on the flake.
Do you have a reference spectrum of pristine graphene on the same substrate? The dose-1 D/G of 0.25 with L_D of about 24 nm might be real residual disorder or a baseline artifact.

limits: The stage-1 relation is valid only for L_D above about 6.2 nm (2 r_A). For dose 4, no defect density can be given from the D/G ratio; its high-density root (L_D ~1.2 nm, n_D ~2e13 cm^-2) lies outside validity and is not a measurement.
I could not verify the n_D = 1e14/(pi L_D^2) conversion from the parsed source text. The absolute densities rest on it, so only the relative trend (~5x increase from dose 1 to dose 3) is robust.

Not verified in this session: Ferrari & Robertson's three-stage model and the Lucchese 2010 form that the Cancado C_A structure is based on. The Lucchese form is inferred from the r_S, r_A, C_S, C_A parameters in the Cancado Fig. 3 caption, not read from an equation.
Not tested: whether the Eckmann I_D/I_D' classification holds at 532 nm (the abstract does not state a laser wavelength).

Only four spectra on one flake at one laser wavelength. No polarization, no temperature series, and no second laser, so the dispersion test used to resolve the two defect-density branches was unavailable.
